political_impact.text: The regulations put the Dominican customs receivership under the Bureau of Insular Affairs and took effect August 1, 1907.

Signed the day the 1907 convention was proclaimed, the order was the domestic housekeeping that put it into operation, after the Senate had let the 1905 treaty die and Roosevelt had run the receivership by a modus vivendi.

reception.text: Critics north and south saw the Roosevelt Corollary as an assertion of hemispheric police power, but the enabling order itself passed without notice.

legacy.text: The receivership remains a textbook example of the Roosevelt Corollary in operation, debated as a milestone of both hemispheric stability and U.S. intervention.

later_actions.text: Executive Order 4353 superseded the 1907 receivership regulations.
The receivership was abolished under the Trujillo–Hull Convention of September 24, 1940.

The 1940 convention terminated automatically after Trujillo proclaimed its end on July 18 and the bondholders were paid toward full redemption; an exchange of notes of August 9, 1951 recognized the termination.

political_impact.text: Per diem employees and day laborers in the federal service, wherever employed, got Labor Day off, as salaried and classified employees already did.

Executive bird reservations were controversial in principle, as ranchers, plume hunters and some in Congress objected to the President locking up land by fiat, but these tiny Louisiana reservations provoked no fight.

legacy.text: The two Louisiana reservations are among the fifty-one bird reservations Roosevelt created by executive order, the practical foundation of the National Wildlife Refuge System.
